macro_news_facts: USDJPY broke above the prior-day 158.25 high and reached at least 158.47-158.49 in Tokyo morning trading.
The move was supported by renewed rise in U.S. 10-year yields toward 5.30% and softer expectations for an imminent BOJ hike.
Brent crude rebounded to about $101.5-$101.7 and WTI to about $90.3, restoring some yen-negative terms-of-trade pressure.
Japan real wages were +1.5% y/y in August, but that yen-supportive macro signal did not prevent USDJPY from making a new local high.
Japan 10-year yield was around 3.07%-3.08% on noncanonical current market pages, below the prior day's 3.093% close.

facts: USDJPY broke above 158.25 and printed at least 158.47-158.49 during Tokyo morning.
Oil prices rebounded above the prior evening levels.
Japan 10-year yields were not rising in tandem and appeared lower than the prior close.
The combination widened the directional pressure toward a weaker yen during the morning.
interpretations: The 09:41 NEUTRAL_TO_SLIGHT_USDJPY_UP view received clear price confirmation after the pair broke the 158.25 resistance area.
The stronger real-wage release failed to generate sustained yen strength, which reinforces the interpretation of limited near-term BOJ-hike repricing.
The return of higher U.S. yields and higher oil adds two simultaneous yen-negative channels.
However, 158.5 and then 159 remain important resistance/intervention-risk zones, so upside conviction should not be escalated to high.
